> [!CAUTION]
> The consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub has been sunset. All code review activity has officially ceased.

The red checks here are the `run-ci` label gate, not test failures. Every failing
job is either `pr-gate` stopping at `Require run-ci label` (the PR has no labels)
or a `*-finish` job reporting that the gate failed. In the `pr-test` run all the
actual test jobs are `skipped`, so nothing in this PR has been exercised yet.

I am not in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, so I cannot add the label myself. Could a
maintainer apply `run-ci` when you get a chance?

The branch still merges cleanly on current main, and nothing has landed in
`disaggregation/decode.py` since the base commit, so no rebase is needed.

commits.messageBody:
_resolve_pending_reqs runs once per scheduler cycle and its pass 2
queried the prefill bootstrap server for every unresolved request with
no rate limit, while pass 1 right above it is throttled to one attempt
per second per bootstrap address.

The prefill registers a room's dp_rank only when it picks the request
up, so until then the decode opened one bootstrap connection per
event-loop iteration. On an idle decode node that is thousands of
connections per second per DP rank, enough to exhaust client ephemeral
ports and stall the handshake.

Throttle the query per bootstrap address the same way pass 1 is
throttled. The interval is 10ms, well under any realistic prefill
scheduling latency, so the first query for a new request is not
delayed.

Fixes #33088
